**The five power stations that are currently the largest in the world (by installed capacity) and the amount that was spent to build them**

| Rank | Power‑station (type) | Country / Location | Installed capacity* | Construction cost (USD) | Approx. cost in local currency* | Year of completion (final unit) | Main sources |
|------|----------------------|--------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------|
| **1** | **Three Gorges Dam** (hydroelectric) | China – Yangtze River, Yichang, Hubei | **22 500 MW** (design‑point) | **US $28–31 billion** (≈ ¥ 200 billion) | ¥ 200 billion (≈ US $30 bn) | 2012 (last turbine) | Wikipedia – “Three Gorges Dam” (cost ≈ ¥ 200 bn, $28 bn ≈ 2012 USD) |
| **2** | **Itaipu Dam** (hydroelectric) | Brazil / Paraguay – Paraná River, border | **14 000 MW** (14 000 MW = 2 × 7 GW units) | **US $19.6 billion** (1991 USD) – about **US $60 billion** in 2023 dollars | US $19.6 bn (original) ≈ R$ 80 bn (1991) | 1984 (final unit) | Wikipedia – “Itaipu Dam” (original cost US $19.6 bn) |
| **3** | **Xiluodu Dam** (hydroelectric) | China – Jinsha River, Yunnan/ Sichuan | **13 860 MW** | **US $8.8 billion** (≈ ¥ 55 billion) | ¥ 55 billion | 2014 (final turbine) | Wikipedia – “Xiluodu Dam” (cost ≈ ¥ 55 bn) |
| **4** | **Jinping‑I Dam** (hydroelectric) | China – Yalong River, Sichuan | **13 700 MW** | **US $12 billion** (≈ ¥ 86 billion) | ¥ 86 billion | 2014 (final unit) | Wikipedia – “Jinping‑I Dam” (cost ≈ ¥ 86 bn) |
| **5** | **Guri Dam** (hydroelectric) | Venezuela – Caroni River, Bolívar | **10 235 MW** | **US $4.5 billion** (1978 USD) – about **US $18 billion** in 2023 dollars | VEF $ 3 billion (original) | 1986 (final unit) | Wikipedia – “Guri Dam” (original cost US $4.5 bn) |

\* **Installed capacity** is the *net* capacity that is currently in commercial operation (not the “design” or “planned” capacity).  
\* **Construction cost** is given in the original currency/value reported in the most reliable source (usually the plant’s Wikipedia article or the operator’s annual report) and, where possible, an approximate 2023‑USD conversion is shown in parentheses.  
\* The figures are rounded to the nearest **hundred million** for readability.

### How the numbers were obtained  

| Power‑station | Where the cost figure comes from |
|---------------|----------------------------------|
| **Three Gorges** | Wikipedia entry “Three Gorges Dam” – the article lists the total project cost as *¥ 200 billion* (≈ US $28 bn at the time of completion) and later estimates of US $30–31 bn when converted to 2023 dollars. |
| **Itaipu** | Wikipedia entry “Itaipu Dam” – the original construction budget is given as *US $19.6 billion* (1991 USD). Inflation calculators give roughly US $60 bn in 2023 dollars. |
| **Xiluodu** | Wikipedia entry “Xiluodu Dam” – cost is quoted as *¥ 55 billion*; using an average 2020‑2023 exchange rate of 6.3 CNY/USD gives about US $8.8 bn. |
| **Jinping‑I** | Wikipedia entry “Jinping‑I Dam” – cost is quoted as *¥ 86 billion*; at 7.2 CNY/USD this is roughly US $12 bn. |
| **Guri** | Wikipedia entry “Guri Dam” – the original cost is listed as *US $4.5 billion* (1978 dollars). Adjusted for inflation to 2023 this is about US $18 bn. |

### Why these five stations are considered the “largest”

* All five rank in the top‑5 of the **“List of largest power stations in the world”** (Wikipedia) when ordered by *current installed capacity*.  
* Three of them (Three Gorges, Itaipu, Xiluodu) are the three biggest **hydroelectric** plants; the remaining two (Jinping‑I and Guri) are also hydro, meaning the current global leaderboard is dominated by hydro‑electric schemes.  
* No coal‑, gas‑, or nuclear‑generated plant yet exceeds the 10 GW threshold; the biggest non‑hydro stations (e.g., China’s Tuoketuo coal plant – 6.7 GW) fall below the fifth‑place hydro plant.

### Quick take‑away

| Plant | Capacity (GW) | Approx. 2023‑USD cost (bn) | Cost per GW |
|-------|---------------|---------------------------|-------------|
| Three Gorges | 22.5 | 30 | **~ 1.3** |
| Itaipu | 14.0 | 60 | **~ 4.3** |
| Xiluodu | 13.9 | 8.8 | **~ 0.6** |
| Jinping‑I | 13.7 | 12 | **~ 0.9** |
| Guri | 10.2 | 18 | **~ 1.8** |

*The “cost per GW” column shows how much was spent (in 2023‑USD) for each gigawatt of installed capacity.  Itaipu’s figure looks high because the original budget was set in the early‑1990s and inflation has dramatically increased its present‑day dollar value.*

---

**If you need more detail** (e.g., breakdown of civil works vs. turbine‑generator cost, financing structure, or a comparison with the largest non‑hydro plants), just let me know and I can dig deeper into the project‑specific reports.
